results.name: parity_match_gap
results.description: Among sets whose examples share one parity (all even or all odd, >=2 examples), yes rate for targets matching that parity minus non-matching; t_observed above null_mean means people weight parity more than the model.
results.code:
# name: parity_match_gap
# description: Among sets whose examples share one parity (all even or all odd, >=2 examples), yes rate for targets matching that parity minus non-matching; t_observed above null_mean means people weight parity more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    par = np.full(len(uniq), -1)
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")]) % 2
        if len(a) >= 2 and (a == a[0]).all():
            par[i] = a[0]
    p = par[codes]
    tp = df["target"].astype(int).values % 2
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    ok = p >= 0
    mt, mn = ok & (tp == p), ok & (tp != p)
    if mt.sum() == 0 or mn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[mt].mean() - r[mn].mean())

results.name: last_digit_share_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets sharing the last digit with at least one but not all examples (multi-example sets); t_observed above null_mean means people use partial surface-digit similarity the model's all-or-none rules ignore.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_share_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets sharing the last digit with at least one but not all examples (multi-example sets); t_observed above null_mean means people use partial surface-digit similarity the model's all-or-none rules ignore.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")])
        if len(a) < 2:
            continue
        idx = np.where(codes == i)[0]
        t = tgt[idx]
        sh = (t[:, None] % 10 == a[None, :] % 10)
        cnt = sh.sum(axis=1)
        notex = ~(t[:, None] == a[None, :]).any(axis=1)
        m[idx] = (cnt >= 1) & (cnt < len(a)) & notex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: far_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets more than 25 away from every example in the set; t_observed above null_mean means people give more distant/rule-based (or noise) yeses than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: far_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets more than 25 away from every example in the set; t_observed above null_mean means people give more distant/rule-based (or noise) yeses than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    d = np.empty(len(df))
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")])
        idx = codes == i
        d[idx] = np.abs(tgt[idx][:, None] - a[None, :]).min(axis=1)
    m = d > 25
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: near_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets within 1-5 of the nearest example; t_observed above null_mean means people show stronger similarity (numerical proximity) generalization than the model.

# name: near_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets within 1-5 of the nearest example; t_observed above null_mean means people show stronger similarity (numerical proximity) generalization than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    d = np.empty(len(df))
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")])
        idx = codes == i
        d[idx] = np.abs(tgt[idx][:, None] - a[None, :]).min(axis=1)
    m = (d >= 1) & (d <= 5)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials where the target is itself one of the shown examples; t_observed below null_mean means people endorse shown examples less than the model (which predicts near-certain yes).

results.name: per_set_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across number_sets of each set's overall yes rate; t_observed above null_mean means people differentiate sets (tight vs broad concepts) more sharply than the model, below means less.

results.name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate in the first third of trial_index minus yes rate in the last third; a nonzero t_observed vs null_mean (~0) means response bias drifts over the session, which the model cannot produce.

results.name: single_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate among trials whose set has exactly one example (target not equal to it); t_observed above null_mean means people generalize more broadly from one example than the model does.
